items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: we would meet up at Warren Smith’s loft up on 21st Street and we would hang out and play until four, five, six in the morning

ctx.x: I mean not the whole time, there was a ten year period where I stopped teaching, but I taught, when I left Philadelphia I was teaching. Matter of fact before I left Philadelphia I taught for two years after I finished college. I finished college in ’66 June and I taught from June of ‘66 through ’67, up until June ’68 in Philadelphia. And in ’68 that’s when I came and moved to New York. But through that whole winter of ’67, September through June, I was driving to New York. I would drive, that was when I was…

player, and that was with Blood, Sweat & Tears. He was the tuba player at the Red Garter. And those were the two gigs in town where you could work steady on the tuba. And so I would come in and do the weekend, I met Howard, we would hang out and I started learning how to improvise and stuff and we would, after he finished the gig at 3:30 I would finish at 3:30, and we would meet up at Warren Smith’s loft up on 21st Street and we would hang out and play until four, five, six in the morning and go to sleep and then…
